title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 69-70
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 69 to 70 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 69 to 70 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 69 to 70.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 69 to 70** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः । त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः केशवः केशिहा हरिः ॥** **कामदेवः कामपालः कामी कान्तः कृतागमः । अनिर्देश्यवपुर्विष्णुर्वीरोऽनन्तो धनञ्जयः ॥**

The hero who slew Kalanemi, Shauri, lord of the brave, is he. The Self of the three worlds and their Lord is that God of gods. Keshava, slayer of Keshi, Hari. He is the God of love, the guardian of every wish, the beloved, the author of the sacred texts. Of a form beyond words, Vishnu is that God of gods. The hero, the endless, Dhananjaya.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 69 to 70 mean?
faq.a: The hero who slew Kalanemi, Shauri, lord of the brave, is he. The Self of the three worlds and their Lord is that God of gods. Keshava, slayer of Keshi, Hari. He is the God of love, the guardian of every wish, the beloved, the author of the sacred texts. Of a form beyond words, Vishnu is that God of gods. The hero, the endless, Dhananjaya.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
